precepts.text: Azariah is named Uzziah, the same king given in greater detail in Chronicles.
precepts.point: Azariah's fuller history is written elsewhere, and the teacher directs the reader to 2 Chronicles 26 for a more detailed account of his life and acts.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

precepts.why:
“Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in the room of his father Amaziah.”

Azariah is Uzziah. Kings says Azariah son of Amaziah was sixteen years old when he began to reign; Chronicles names the same king Uzziah and gives his life and acts in greater detail. Kings itself points there: “are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?” For the fuller account of the king who did right, left the high places standing, and was smitten a leper, read 2 Chronicles 26.

precepts.text: The Most High promised Jehu that his children of the fourth generation would sit on Israel's throne, fulfilled in Zachariah.
precepts.point: The end of Zachariah fulfills the word spoken to Jehu, that his sons would sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

precepts.why:
The Most High told Jehu, “Because thou hast done well in executing that which is right in mine eyes, and hast done unto the house of Ahab according to all that was in mine heart, thy children of the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel.”

Zachariah the son of Jeroboam is that fourth generation. He reigned six months, did evil, departed not from the sins of Jeroboam, and Shallum conspired against him and slew him. And Kings says it outright: “This was the word of the Lord which he spake unto Jehu, saying, Thy sons shall sit on the throne of Israel unto the fourth generation. And so it came to pass.”

precepts.text: Tiglathpileser king of Assyria carries away the northern regions captive to Assyria, the first transporting of Israel out of the land.
precepts.point: The hatred carried straight through the history. Elisha would not even look toward the king of Israel and dealt only with Jehoshaphat of Judah, and later Pekah of Israel conspired with Rezin of Syria against Judah, which began the exile of the north by the Assyrian kings.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“In the days of Pekah king of Israel came Tiglath–pileser king of Assyria, and took Ijon, and Abel–beth–maachah, and Janoah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and carried them captive to Assyria.”

That is the first transporting of Israel out of the land. The Assyrian kings began the exile of the northern kingdom in the days of Pekah.

points: Came Tiglathpileser king of Assyria and carried them captive to Assyria. This is what we were reading about in the book of Amos earlier.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: Azariah, also called Uzziah, begins to reign over Judah and does that which is right in the sight of the Most High as his father Amaziah had done.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: The high places were not removed, so the people still sacrificed and burned incense there, an incomplete obedience.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: The Most High smote him so that he was a leper until his death, and he dwelt in a separate house while Jotham his son judged the people.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: Azariah's fuller history is written elsewhere, and the teacher directs the reader to 2 Chronicles 26 for a more detailed account of his life and acts.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: Zachariah son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel only six months and does that which is evil, not departing from the sins of Jeroboam.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: Shallum conspires against Zachariah, smites him before the people, slays him, and reigns in his place.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: The end of Zachariah fulfills the word spoken to Jehu, that his sons would sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: Shallum reigns a full month in Samaria before Menahem son of Gadi goes up from Tirzah, smites him, and reigns in his stead.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: Menahem strikes Tiphsah and its coasts because they would not open to him, and he ripped up the women with child, a mark of his cruelty.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: Menahem reigns ten years in Samaria and does evil, not departing from the sins of Jeroboam.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: Pul the king of Assyria comes against the land, and Menahem gives him a thousand talents of silver to confirm the kingdom in his hand.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: Menahem raises the tribute by exacting fifty shekels of silver from each mighty man of wealth, so the king of Assyria turns back and does not stay in the land.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: Pekahiah son of Menahem reigns two years over Israel and does evil, not departing from the sins of Jeroboam.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: Pekah, a captain of his, conspires against him and smites him in the king's house at Samaria with fifty Gileadites, then reigns in his room.
This is a military coup, where a trusted captain kills the king and seizes the throne.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: Pekah son of Remaliah reigns twenty years over Israel, the same Pekah spoken of in the book of Isaiah.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: In his days Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria comes and takes Ijon, Abel-beth-maachah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee, and all the land of Naphtali, carrying them captive to Assyria.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: Hoshea son of Elah conspires against Pekah, smites and slays him, and reigns in his stead.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: Jotham son of Uzziah reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem and does that which is right, according to all his father Uzziah had done.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: Again the high places were not removed, and the people still sacrificed and burned incense there.
Jotham builds the higher gate of the house of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: In those days the Most High begins to send Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.
